I am a 63-year-old woman. I have never been to school. I cannot read. But I know my land. I have farmed these 7 and a half mu for 40 years — since I was 23. My husband and I, we are the only ones left in the house now. Our children have gone to the city. It is just us two old people.

We have 5 mu that we do wheat and maize on, year after year. That is our main field. The other 2 and a half mu we plant cotton. That has been our way for as long as I can remember. The wheat and maize keep us fed. The cotton gives us a little cash for medicine and for the New Year.

**Wheat (5 mu):** I will plant the wheat around October 10th, when the autumn rain comes and the soil is soft. I use the seed we saved from last year — the same kind my mother-in-law used. Why change? It grows. Before planting, my husband plows with the small tractor, and I spread the fertilizer. I put about half a bag of that compound fertilizer on each mu — the kind with three numbers on it, though I cannot read them. The shop man knows what I mean. Then in March or April, when the wheat turns a bit yellow after winter, I topdress with urea. Maybe one more bag for the whole 5 mu. I will irrigate twice — once after planting if it is dry, and once in spring. The well water is metered now, so I do not waste it. For weeds, I spray once after planting. I do not hire anyone. We cut the wheat ourselves in early June with a small machine we borrow from my nephew. I expect about 380 kg per mu. Last year was about the same.

**Maize (5 mu):** The wheat comes off in early June, and we have no time! We must plant the maize within a few days. I buy the yellow hybrid seed from the supply store. It costs more, but the seed we save does not grow well for maize — I learned that long ago. We put fertilizer in the holes when we plant — about the same as wheat, maybe a little more. One more time we fertilize when the maize is tall. I irrigate once, maybe twice if the summer is very hot. I spray for weeds once. Harvest is in late September. I expect about 420 kg per mu. If the rain is good, maybe 450. If not, 380. You never know.

**Cotton (2 and a half mu):** We plant the cotton in mid-April. Cotton needs warm soil. I use the seed we saved — the white fluffy kind. I put down less fertilizer than wheat, maybe one bag of compound for the whole 2 and a half mu, and some urea when the flowers come. Cotton needs more watching. I spray for bugs three or four times — the bollworms come every year. I irrigate twice, once when it is young and once when it flowers. Picking takes forever. We do it by hand, going back again and again from September to October. With only 2 and a half mu, we can manage. I do not hire workers — we have no money for that. I expect about 200 kg of lint per mu, but I think more in terms of the seed cotton. It should be enough.

**Money:** Everything is about what we can afford. We do not buy the best fertilizer. We do not irrigate more than we must because the electricity for the pump costs too much. We do what we have always done. It is not perfect, but we survive. My husband wanted to try more fertilizer last year because the neighbor did, but I said no — we do not have the cash, and what if the price drops? Better to be a little safe. We are old. We cannot afford a bad year.
